sources.title: GHC CPP compiler-version predicates
sources.version_or_date: GHC 7.10.2; official manual date 2015-07-22 corroborated by a search excerpt, not an opened dated PDF
sources.sections_read: 4.12.3 Options affecting the C pre-processor; 4.12.4 custom preprocessor pipeline.
sources.confirmed: GHC supplies compiler-version macros and a minimum-version predicate for CPP, with an existence guard for older compilers. Custom preprocessing runs before the Haskell compiler proper.
sources.limits: Older compilers may lack the predicate, so its presence needs guarding; external CPP also interacts with language-specific string syntax. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C26.json.

sources.title: C/C++ preprocessing with a language-standard version macro
sources.version_or_date: GCC 5.3.0; release dated 2015-12-04 by the opened official release history
sources.confirmed: Language-standard macros expose numeric versions, and __cplusplus varies with the selected language standard. This supplies a concrete guard input for source compatibility.
sources.limits: A transferred design must skip incompatible grammar before parsing; excluded text may still need valid tokenization, and compiler release is distinct from selected language mode. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C26.json.

sources.version_or_date: Clang 3.7.0; official LLVM release announcement dated 2015-09-01 opened separately
sources.confirmed: Clang distinguishes features enabled by the selected standard from extensions and demonstrates compatibility definitions for compilers lacking its feature-query macros.
sources.limits: Feature names and fallback behavior require a stable contract, and older compilers must understand the guarding mechanism.
